science_relevance.scientific_problem: Plan short delivery routes that serve customer demands without exceeding vehicle capacity.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: This problem represents resource and distance constraints in distribution logistics. Research seeks better feasible delivery plans; local synthetic instances are a controlled subproblem rather than measured real-world savings.

papers.title: Hybrid Genetic Search for the CVRP: Open-Source Implementation and SWAP* Neighborhood
papers.task_relation: Vidal develops and evaluates an algorithm specifically to solve capacitated vehicle routing. Capacitated vehicle routing has a different candidate interface, but its distance objective and demand/capacity constraints pursue the same logistics problem.
papers.primary_goal: Improve feasible low-cost solutions of the capacitated vehicle-routing problem.

science_relevance.reason: Primary research addresses the underlying problem directly; scientific importance does not rely on the agent/framework paper.
science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
